title: Choosing, storing and transporting cartridges
summary: Which cartridges to take for Sporting™, Compak® Sporting and practice, how to store them safely and what to know about transport. Limits differ between countries and airlines.

body.html: For Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™ many shooters choose 28 g with No. 7½ or No. 8 shot: such a cartridge handles both close and far targets. Some also keep No. 9 cartridges in the vest for close targets.

In Compak® Sporting the targets are mostly at medium range, so 24–28 g with No. 8 or No. 7½ is popular, with No. 9 for close targets. Chokes are not changed within a round there, so you choose cartridges and chokes together for the whole round.

For practice 24 g is a good choice: cheaper, softer and less tiring. Many coaches suggest keeping to one brand and model, so that recoil and pattern feel the same. Before a competition, practise with the cartridges you will compete with.

Before a trip, ask the organiser which cartridges the ground allows: fibre wads are often required, and sometimes only steel shot with a size limit. And bring plenty: in both disciplines you must come to the stand with enough cartridges for the whole round.

Store cartridges in a dry, cool place, away from heat, sun and open flame, in their original boxes, locked up and out of reach of children. In many countries the law requires cartridges to be stored separately from the gun and limits how many you may keep at home.

By car, cartridges travel in their original boxes, in many countries separately from the gun. By plane they travel in checked baggage only, with the airline's approval, up to 5 kg per person including packaging, for your own use, securely packed. People travelling together cannot pool their limits, and many airlines allow less or refuse ammunition altogether.
Never put cartridges in hand luggage or in your pockets when you fly. More about flying and about buying cartridges on site: Flying with a gun and Buying cartridges at the destination.

key_points.html: Sporting™: often 28 g No. 7½ or No. 8; Compak® Sporting: 24–28 g No. 8 or No. 7½.
Practice: 24 g and one brand of cartridge.
Check the ground's rules in advance: fibre wads, steel, shot size.
Store dry, cool, locked up, out of reach of children.
Flying: cartridges travel in checked baggage only, with the airline's approval, up to 5 kg per person including packaging, for your own use; airlines may be stricter.

did_you_know.html: On a trip it is often simplest to buy cartridges at the club on site: they meet the ground's rules, and you do not have to fly with them.

quiz.q: Which cartridge do many shooters choose for Sporting™?
quiz.explain: 28 g with No. 7½ or No. 8 shot is an all-round choice within the FITASC rules. 36 g, 32 g and No. 6 are outside them, and No. 11 (about 1.5 mm) is below the 2.0 mm minimum.

quiz.q: Where are cartridges not allowed on a plane?

options.text: In hand luggage or in pockets

quiz.explain: Cartridges travel only in checked baggage, securely packed and with the airline's approval.

options.text: Dry, cool, locked, away from children
In the car, where it is warm and sunny
Next to a heater, so they stay dry
Loose in the pockets of a jacket

quiz.explain: Heat and damp spoil cartridges; locked up, they are out of reach of children and strangers.
